issues: P1 — Cleanup remains interruptible after registration. bounded_process restores the original signal mask before monitoring, and its finally block calls terminate_group without blocking SIGTERM/SIGINT. If an ordinary exception already initiated final cleanup, one handled signal during its sleeps or proc.wait raises KeyboardInterrupt and aborts cleanup. Similarly, another handled signal during cleanup after an initial interruption can leave live workers behind. The outer finally restores the mask but does not finish cleanup, and exclusive_lock subsequently releases the writer lock. stop_recovered_group has the same interruptible teardown pattern. Repair: defer handled termination throughout teardown, retain ownership and the lock until quiescence or a durably recorded unresolved-cleanup veto, then restore the original mask and propagate interruption. Add focused coverage for interruption during exception-path cleanup and repeated interruption during shutdown; the supplied registration-deferral test name does not establish these cases.

P2 — stop_recovered_group can leak an acquired pidfd on an identity-read exception. After open_pidfd succeeds, the descriptor is not added to descriptors until process_identity and identity validation finish. If that read raises, for example ProcessLookupError during process exit or an I/O error, the outer finally cannot close this descriptor. Repair: register descriptor ownership immediately after acquisition, or use a per-descriptor try/finally that closes it unless ownership transfers to descriptors. Handle disappearance consistently as a vanished process while preserving fail-closed treatment of other identity-read failures. Verify that every successfully opened descriptor closes on validation failure and exception.
next_actions: Make teardown signal-deferral and pidfd ownership exception-safe.

residuals: Recovery takes one membership snapshot. A trusted worker that forks during shutdown can leave an unsignalled descendant; the final membership check correctly vetoes continuation. This is a fail-closed recovery limitation, not false completion.
Recovery allows only 0.1 seconds after SIGKILL before checking membership, so scheduling or delayed kernel exit can cause a conservative veto.
